meta.title: Fran Barahona — Product Engineer
meta.description: Product-minded software engineer. Responsible for the web platform at Webel, with a full-stack foundation in Ruby on Rails from AuroraJobs.
meta.ogImageAlt: Fran Barahona, Product Engineer. Problem, specification, build, review, delivery.

hero.title: Product Engineer
hero.subtitle: My responsibility is technical: whole web surfaces and the architecture under them. I work close to product and hand part of the implementation to agents; the specification and the review are mine.
hero.context: Responsible for the web platform at Webel. Full-stack foundation in Ruby on Rails at AuroraJobs.

summary.title: Technical ownership of products in production
facts: At Webel I run all of web: the B2C app thousands of people use every day, the B2B platform, the internal dashboard, SEO, email, and the shared library.
At AuroraJobs I built the whole application in Rails and mentored and coordinated a team of two developers.
I work with agents from specifications and reusable skills. The code, the tests, and the final call are mine.

projects.title: Lab
projects.intro: Prototypes and utilities I build on my own initiative. Each one tests a specific idea and states where it actually stands, without posing as paid work.

selectedWork.title: Two products, two kinds of ownership
selectedWork.intro: Each case covers the problem, the part I owned, two or three decisions, and what changed afterwards.

principles.title: How I work with agents

items.title: Define the problem
items.description: I work out who it is for, what needs to change, and the smallest solution worth building. I write down scope, constraints, and acceptance criteria.

items.title: Set up the work
items.description: I split implementation into reviewable parts and give each agent the context it needs. Reusable skills and design-system docs keep technical decisions from getting lost between tasks.

items.title: Review and validate
items.description: I review the code, tests, and outcome against the specification. When a choice affects the product or architecture, I make it and update the context before work continues.

artifacts: Reusable skills that capture technical decisions and quality criteria.
Specifications with scope, constraints, and acceptance criteria written before implementation.

experience.title: Webel and AuroraJobs
experience.evolutionNote: AuroraJobs gave me my full-stack foundation and a two-developer team to coordinate. At Webel I run the whole web area and the architecture its products share.
